_comment: Promoted from daf, the only site that had an accessibility gate at all.
The chromeLaunchConfig args and the 60s timeout are verbatim: the timeout
pairs with the navigation-timeout escape in the workflow, which tells a
transport flake apart from a real violation and warns loudly instead of
failing silently. That escape is well judged and is kept as written.
The ignore list is NOT settled. Suppressing color-contrast on a site read
by ten-year-olds is not an accessibility programme, and duplicate-id is a
real defect wherever it appears. Both stay for now only because F2 has
just changed every surface colour and turning contrast on in the same
release would produce a wall of failures with no way to tell a token bug
from a content one. Gate C14 removes them, after one release at warn.
Route scope is C14's business too: this audits /materials/ alone today.
